title: White for harvest (John 4:31–38)
hookLine: lift up your eyes: the fields are already white

lines: I HAVE FOOD YOU DON'T KNOW.
cards: The disciples come back from town with lunch and find Jesus talking with a Samaritan woman. They're surprised, but nobody asks. She leaves her water jar right there and hurries back into town.
Come, and see a man who has told me all things whatsoever I have done. Is not he the Christ? Meanwhile the disciples unpack the food.
Rabbi, eat. And he says something that makes them look at each other: I have food to eat that you don't know about. Did someone already bring him lunch?

teach.h: MY FOOD IS TO DO HIS WILL.
teach.b: This is John's pattern: Jesus says something deep, and someone takes it at ground level. Born again: back into the womb? Living water: where's your bucket?
Food: who brought him a sandwich? Then he explains, in the Douay-Rheims: "My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, that I may perfect his work." Meat is the old word for food.
What feeds him is doing his Father's will. Then he points.
You have a saying, he tells them: four more months, and then the harvest. Farmers' wisdom.
"Behold, I say to you, lift up your eyes, and see the countries, for they are white already to harvest." Countries here means the fields. White, because grain goes pale and gold when it's ripe.
But picture what the disciples might see when they look up: the Samaritans the woman has just told, coming out of the town through the grain.
Some readers have wondered whether the white was the light clothing of that crowd. The text doesn't say. Either way, the harvest isn't four months off.
Then: one sows and another reaps; you are reaping where others did the hard work.
Readers name many sowers: the prophets, John the Baptist, Jesus himself. And here, in a small way, the woman with her jar, the last worker the disciples would have picked.

how: Catholics hear this passage as part of the longer Gospel of the Samaritan woman on the Third Sunday of Lent in Year A, and the Church has often drawn on it in teaching about the mission to share the faith.

games.q: you're a disciple. you've brought back lunch, and Jesus says the harvest is ready now, not in four months. you lift your eyes. what do you see?
o: people from the town, coming toward you.
games.why: the Samaritans, told by the woman, are coming out of the town. the harvest isn't four months away. it's walking up the road.

practice: Lift your eyes, literally: look up from the screen, at the room, out the window.
Then let the people in your week pass through your mind, and notice who seems open, lonely, curious or ready for a kind word, maybe someone you'd never have picked.
If you pray, pray for them by name; if not, just keep one face in mind.

wordCard.voice: White for harvest. Fields pale and ripe, ready now, not in four months: Jesus's picture of the Samaritans coming to hear him. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: white, pale (John 4:35), the color of grain ripe for harvest.

carryVoice: Your line: lift up your eyes. The fields are ready now, not in four months. Day five hundred one.
